## Test Case: AUTH-A11Y-001

**Test Case ID:** AUTH-A11Y-001
**Title:** All login form fields are accessible via keyboard Tab navigation
**Priority:** P1
**Module:** Authentication — Accessibility — Keyboard Navigation
**Scenario Type:** Accessibility
**Risk Level:** High
**Tags:** @Accessibility, @Auth, @P1, @Keyboard, @WCAG2.1-AA, @SC2.1.1

**Preconditions:**
- User is on the login page
- Keyboard-only navigation mode

**Test Steps:**
1. Navigate to the login page
2. Use Tab key to navigate through all interactive elements
3. Verify each focusable element receives keyboard focus
4. Use Shift+Tab to navigate backwards
5. Press Enter on the Login button using keyboard only

**Expected Results:**
- Email field, Password field, Login button, and all links receive focus in logical order
- Tab order follows visual layout (left-to-right, top-to-bottom)
- Shift+Tab reverses focus correctly
- No keyboard traps (user can Tab through and out of all elements)
- Login can be completed entirely without a mouse
- Focus indicator is visible on each element (WCAG 2.4.7)

## Test Case: AUTH-A11Y-002

**Test Case ID:** AUTH-A11Y-002
**Title:** Login form fields have visible focus indicators meeting minimum contrast
**Priority:** P1
**Module:** Authentication — Accessibility — Focus Indicators
**Scenario Type:** Accessibility
**Risk Level:** High
**Tags:** @Accessibility, @Auth, @P1, @FocusIndicator, @WCAG2.1-AA, @SC2.4.7

**Preconditions:**
- User is on the login page

**Test Steps:**
1. Use Tab key to focus on the Email input field
2. Observe the focus ring/outline
3. Tab to Password field
4. Tab to Login button
5. Tab to any links on the page

**Expected Results:**
- Each focused element has a clearly visible focus indicator (outline, border, background change)
- Focus indicator contrast ratio meets WCAG minimum (3:1 against adjacent colors)
- Focus indicator is not removed by CSS (`outline: none` without alternative)
- Focus ring is at least 2px in width

## Test Case: AUTH-A11Y-003

**Test Case ID:** AUTH-A11Y-003
**Title:** Login form labels are correctly associated with input fields
**Priority:** P1
**Module:** Authentication — Accessibility — Form Labels
**Scenario Type:** Accessibility
**Risk Level:** High
**Tags:** @Accessibility, @Auth, @P1, @FormLabels, @ScreenReader, @WCAG2.1-AA, @SC1.3.1

**Preconditions:**
- User is on the login page
- Screen reader or accessibility audit tool available

**Test Steps:**
1. Navigate to the login page
2. Inspect the HTML: check `<label for="">` associations with `<input id="">`
3. Run automated accessibility scan (axe-core or similar)
4. Simulate screen reader focus on each input field

**Expected Results:**
- Email input has `<label for="email">Email</label>` or equivalent `aria-label`
- Password input has `<label for="password">Password</label>` or equivalent
- Screen reader announces field name when focused: "Email, edit text" or similar
- Placeholder text is NOT used as the sole label (placeholders disappear on input)
- `aria-required="true"` is set on mandatory fields

## Test Case: AUTH-A11Y-004

**Test Case ID:** AUTH-A11Y-004
**Title:** Login error messages are announced by screen readers via ARIA live regions
**Priority:** P1
**Module:** Authentication — Accessibility — Error Announcements
**Scenario Type:** Accessibility
**Risk Level:** High
**Tags:** @Accessibility, @Auth, @P1, @ARIA, @LiveRegion, @ScreenReader, @WCAG2.1-AA, @SC3.3.1

**Preconditions:**
- User is on the login page
- Screen reader active or ARIA audit tool available

**Test Steps:**
1. Navigate to login page
2. Submit the form with empty fields
3. Observe how validation errors are presented
4. Check if error messages are announced without moving focus manually
5. Inspect HTML for `aria-live`, `role="alert"`, or `aria-describedby`

**Expected Results:**
- Validation errors are announced automatically by screen reader
- Error messages are in an `aria-live="polite"` or `role="alert"` region
- Each field's error is associated with the field via `aria-describedby`
- Error icon (if used) has `aria-hidden="true"` (visual only) or descriptive `aria-label`
- Color is NOT the only way errors are indicated (also text and icon)

## Test Case: AUTH-A11Y-005

**Test Case ID:** AUTH-A11Y-005
**Title:** Login page text meets WCAG 2.1 AA color contrast ratio (4.5:1)
**Priority:** P1
**Module:** Authentication — Accessibility — Color Contrast
**Scenario Type:** Accessibility
**Risk Level:** High
**Tags:** @Accessibility, @Auth, @P1, @ColorContrast, @WCAG2.1-AA, @SC1.4.3

**Preconditions:**
- User is on the login page
- Color contrast analysis tool available (browser extension or axe-core)

**Test Steps:**
1. Navigate to the login page
2. Run color contrast analysis on:
   - Label text vs. background
   - Placeholder text vs. input background
   - Button text vs. button background
   - Link text vs. page background
   - Error message text vs. background
3. Record contrast ratios

**Expected Results:**
- Regular text (< 18pt): contrast ratio ≥ 4.5:1
- Large text (≥ 18pt or bold 14pt): contrast ratio ≥ 3:1
- Input placeholders: ≥ 4.5:1 (WCAG 2.1 requirement)
- Button text against button color: ≥ 4.5:1
- Error text (often red): ≥ 4.5:1 on white/light background
- No automated contrast failures reported by axe-core

## Test Case: AUTH-A11Y-006

**Test Case ID:** AUTH-A11Y-006
**Title:** Login page heading hierarchy is logical (H1 before H2 before H3)
**Priority:** P2
**Module:** Authentication — Accessibility — Heading Structure
**Scenario Type:** Accessibility
**Risk Level:** Medium
**Tags:** @Accessibility, @Auth, @P2, @Headings, @DocumentStructure, @WCAG2.1-AA, @SC1.3.1

**Preconditions:**
- User is on the login page

**Test Steps:**
1. Navigate to the login page
2. Inspect HTML heading structure
3. Verify headings appear in correct order without skipping levels

**Expected Results:**
- Page has exactly one `<h1>` (the main page heading, e.g., "Sign In")
- Subheadings use `<h2>`, `<h3>` in nested order
- No heading levels are skipped (e.g., no H4 without H3 above it)
- Heading text meaningfully describes the section content

## Test Case: AUTH-A11Y-007

**Test Case ID:** AUTH-A11Y-007
**Title:** Login page is fully operable at 200% browser zoom without horizontal scrolling
**Priority:** P2
**Module:** Authentication — Accessibility — Reflow
**Scenario Type:** Accessibility
**Risk Level:** Medium
**Tags:** @Accessibility, @Auth, @P2, @Zoom, @Reflow, @WCAG2.1-AA, @SC1.4.4

**Preconditions:**
- User is on the login page
- Browser zoom controls available

**Test Steps:**
1. Navigate to the login page at 100% zoom
2. Increase browser zoom to 200% (Ctrl/Cmd + to 200%)
3. Attempt to complete the login flow at 200% zoom

**Expected Results:**
- Login page reflows correctly at 200% zoom
- No horizontal scrollbar appears
- All form fields and buttons remain accessible
- Text does not overflow outside containers
- Login can be completed successfully at 200% zoom
